title: Model a queue visibility lease
statement:
Step 8 · Reliable writes

A visibility lease temporarily hides a polled message. If processing fails and the lease expires, the message becomes eligible again: at-least-once delivery needs idempotent consumers. This simplified queue uses message IDs for acknowledgements; real systems need receipt tokens to reject stale acknowledgements.

Build it

Simulate enqueue(id,time), poll(time), and ack(id,time). Return an ID or None for each poll. Pick the earliest enqueued currently visible message, then hide it until poll_time+lease. Ack removes the ID. IDs are unique; operations are time-ordered and lease is positive.

Contract: Implement queue using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: operations = [["enqueue", "a", 0], ["enqueue", "b", 0], ["poll", 0], ["poll", 0], ["poll", 1], ["poll", 5], ["ack", "a", 5], ["poll", 5]], lease = 5
Expected: ["a", "b", null, "a", "b"]
Input: operations = [], lease = 3
Expected: []
Hint

Track a visible-again time for each message and retain original enqueue order.

Review your understanding

Why is an ack by ID unsafe when a lease expires and another worker receives the message?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
